rows.jp: あれで没ってことは、どう攻めたらいいんだろう。
rows.en: If that one got rejected, what angle was I supposed to try next?

ghs.en: She failed that other one, so what is a good way of attacking now?
ghs.assessment: The source says the previous script was rejected and wonders how to approach the next attempt. The English makes Senpai the person who failed, rather than the evaluator who rejected his work.
ghs.remedy: Use 'If that one was rejected, how should I approach the next?'

ghs.assessment: The source's implicit possessor is the narrator: his hand will not move. The definite phrase sounds like a detached or previously identified hand.
ghs.remedy: Use 'My hand won't move.'

rows.jp: タンスの中から、着流しを取り出し、着替える。
rows.en: I pulled a kimono from the dresser and slipped it on.

ghs.en: Out of the dresser I produce a men's Kimono, and in Kinigashi style, casually dress with it.
ghs.assessment: The English is ungrammatical, misspells the garment style, and treats the source's casual kimono outfit as both a separate men's kimono and a style applied afterward.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I take a casual kimono from the dresser and change into it.'

highlights.text: produce a men's Kimono, and in Kinigashi style, casually dress with it

ghs.en: Taichi: "...the explosive birth of a master at literature."
ghs.assessment: The source's comic proclamation is that a literary master has been born. 'Master at literature' is not idiomatic English.
ghs.remedy: Use 'A literary master is born with a bang.'

ghs.en: Because the mood is very important,

rows.jp: そんなことをやっていると。
rows.en: While I was carrying on like that—

ghs.en: that is what I must do.
ghs.assessment: The source is a temporal transition, 'As I was doing that...' The English instead states an obligation and breaks the arrival sequence.
ghs.remedy: Use 'As I was doing that...'

highlights.text: that is what I must do

rows.en: The voice came from the entryway.

rows.jp: 突如とした現れた着物の男に、友貴はびびったようだった。
rows.en: Tomoki flinched when a man in a kimono suddenly materialized in front of him.

ghs.en: Tomoki seemed to jitter in surprise at the sight of a man in Kimono materializing in front of him all of a sudden.
ghs.assessment: Materialized can idiomatically describe a sudden appearance and need not imply a supernatural arrival. The confirmed defect is the malformed reaction phrase jitter in surprise at the sight of.
ghs.remedy: Say naturally that Tomoki flinched or looked startled when the kimono-clad man appeared.

highlights.text: jitter in surprise at the sight of a man in Kimono materializing in front of him

ghs.assessment: The source colloquially means 'Leave me alone' or 'Shut up.' The formal command to leave a place has the wrong object and register.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Leave me alone.'

ghs.en: Tomoki: "My mistake. I mean, what's that figure..."
ghs.assessment: The source corrects 'face' to 'outfit' or 'getup.' 'Figure' refers to body shape or a person and misses the clothing joke.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I mean, what's with that outfit?'

rows.jp: 「本当に間違いなのかそれは？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Truly a mistake what you made?"
ghs.assessment: The question lacks an auxiliary and has malformed word order. The source asks whether the first remark was really a mistake.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Was that really a mistake?'

highlights.text: Truly a mistake what you made

rows.jp: 「ジャパニーズキモーノだな」

ghs.en: Tomoki: "It's a Japanese Kimono, isn't it."

rows.jp: 「ジャパニーズソーセキでもある」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Also the habits of the Japanese Soseki."
ghs.assessment: The source extends the 'Japanese kimono' phrasing into a self-identification with the literary figure Soseki. The English invents his habits and loses the speaker's comic claim.
ghs.remedy: Preserve the parallel as 'And Japanese Soseki, too.'

highlights.text: the habits of the Japanese Soseki

ghs.assessment: The source merely reacts that Soseki is impressive. The English explicitly labels the preceding line a pun, adding interpretation to the dialogue.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Soseki, huh... impressive.'

rows.jp: 友貴はよりいっそう俺を尊敬したようだった。
rows.en: Tomoki looked more impressed with me than ever.

ghs.en: Seems Tomoki's respect for me has further grown.
ghs.assessment: The surrounding narration reports a completed impression in the past. The present perfect breaks that time frame.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Tomoki seemed to respect me even more.'

rows.jp: 着たのは二度目なのだけど。
rows.en: Though this was only the second time I had worn it.

ghs.en: This is only the second time I have worn this though.

rows.jp: 「で、こんな夜更けにどうした」
rows.en: “So what brings you here at this hour?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "So, what is your purpose this late in the evening?"

rows.jp: 「いや……どうしたもこうしたも……これ、太一の分」
rows.en: “What do you mean, what brings me? Here—your share.”

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Well... purpose, now, let's say, ah... here, Taichi, your part."
ghs.assessment: The English is incoherent. The source dismisses the question as nothing special and presents Taichi with his share.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Nothing special... Here, this is your share.'

highlights.text: purpose, now, let's say, ah... here, Taichi, your part

rows.jp: 「中身は……暗くてよく見えないな」
rows.en: “What’s inside...? It’s too dark to tell.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "What's inside... it's too dark, I can't see well."

rows.jp: 「部活のおすそわけだよ。夏場だし、無駄に抱えてても腐るしさ」
rows.en: “A little something from the club. It’s summer, and if we keep more than we need, it’ll rot.”

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Your part of the loot from club activities. It's summertime now, so keeping this stuff around is a waste 'cause it just spoils."

ghs.assessment: The following sentence does identify the thumbs-up, so the action is not lost from the passage. The isolated Tahm nevertheless supplies an opaque invented sound where the emphatic mimetic beat should make the gesture immediately legible.
ghs.remedy: Use a compact gesture cue such as (Thumbs up.).

rows.jp: 俺たちは不敵に笑いつつ、親指を立てあった。
rows.en: We traded fearless grins and a thumbs-up.

ghs.en: We laughed fearlessly as we stuck our thumbs up.

rows.jp: 「黒須太一は、青春純情ボーイ・島友貴を応援します」
rows.en: “Taichi Kurosu proudly supports Tomoki Shima, the wholesome face of youth.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Kurosu Taichi shall be cheering for you, 『Boy of Pure-hearted Adolescence * Shima Tomoki!』"

ghs.assessment: The source corrects the wording to say she was found collapsed or had collapsed. The English progressive describes an ongoing or repeated act of fainting.
ghs.remedy: Use 'More precisely, she was found collapsed.'

rows.jp: 「あいつはハラキリ拳の使い手で、俺のカラデをもってしても倒すのは容易じゃないはずだ」
rows.en: “She’s a master of Harakiri Fist. Not even my karade could take her down that easily.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "That one is the master of the Harakiri Fist, that even I with my Karade do not expect to make her part with her senses!"
ghs.assessment: The source has Taichi misunderstand 'collapsed' as 'defeated' and boast that even his Karade would struggle to defeat her. The English is ungrammatical and collapses the joke back into loss of consciousness.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Even with my Karade, she wouldn't be easy to defeat.'

highlights.text: that even I with my Karade do not expect to make her part with her senses

rows.jp: 「その倒れた違う。それにカラデってのもわけわからないし」
rows.en: “Wrong kind of ‘down.’ And I still have no idea what karade is.”

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Not 'fainting' because of that! And that Karade's something incomprehensible, by the way."

rows.jp: 「そんでさ……今は桜庭が看護してるんだけど、当然役に立たないから……支倉先輩に看てもらえないかなって」
rows.en: “Anyway... Sakuraba’s looking after her now, but obviously he’s no help, so... could you ask Hasekura to take a look at her?”

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Anyway... right now Sakuraba's looking after her, but naturally he's useless, so... is Hasekura-senpai available to nurse her?"
Tomoki: "Could you ask her right away?"

rows.jp: 「ああ、じゃちょっと行ってくるわ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Yeah, I'll be back in a while, yes."

rows.jp: サンダルをはいて、彼女の家に向かう。
rows.en: I slipped on my sandals and headed to her house.

ghs.en: I wear my sandals and I head towards her house.
ghs.assessment: The source narrates completed actions in sequence. The English shifts to simple present and uses 'wear' where 'put on' is required for the action.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I put on my sandals and headed for her house.'

highlights.text: I wear my sandals and I head

rows.jp: 戻ってくると、まだ友貴がいた。
rows.en: When I returned, Tomoki was still there.

ghs.en: When I returned back, still Tomoki was there.
ghs.assessment: 'Returned back' is redundant, and the following adverbial inversion is unidiomatic. The source says Tomoki was still there when the narrator returned.
ghs.remedy: Use 'When I came back, Tomoki was still there.'

highlights.text: returned back, still Tomoki was there

rows.en: “She said yes. She’s already on her way.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "She said OK. She's on her way already."

rows.jp: 「太一の言うことだけはよく聞くんだ」

ghs.en: Tomoki: "She only really does what you tell her to, Taichi."

rows.jp: 「そうしないといろいろエラーが起こるからな」
rows.en: “Otherwise all kinds of errors crop up.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "If she didn't, there would be many many errors happening all around."

rows.jp: 「それより、あがって９８（キュッパチ）でゲームでもやってく？」
rows.en: “Never mind that. Want to come in and play something on the PC-98?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "So anyway, wanna come in and play a game with the 98 (pronounced 'kyuppachi')?"

ghs.assessment: The fragment uses a demonstrative as though replying to a named object. The source adds the aside that he does not actually own a PC-98.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Though I don't have one.'

rows.jp: 「おまえ、ディスク交換担当ね」

ghs.en: Taichi: "You're in charge of disk swap."

rows.jp: 「嘘だと言ってくれよ、マイフレン」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Mai furendo, what you just told me must be a lie."
ghs.assessment: マイフレン is deliberately clipped, not an ordinary loan rendering of my friend; it begins a malformed-language and surname-joke chain. Expanding it to Mai furendo removes the clipping that makes the mechanism work.
ghs.remedy: Preserve an intelligibly clipped English form that can support the following malformed-language joke.

ghs.en: Tomoki: "...you tryin' to flash kick my thoughts?"

rows.jp: 友貴のギャグはこんなのばかりだ。
rows.en: That was the only kind of joke Tomoki ever made.

ghs.en: Tomoki's gags are all like this.

rows.jp: パソコン少年の分際で。

ghs.en: When his social class is that of a PC guy!
ghs.assessment: The source taunts him for not knowing despite being a computer kid. The English invents a social-class claim and loses the concessive rebuke.
ghs.remedy: Use 'And you call yourself a computer kid.'

highlights.text: social class is that of a PC guy

rows.jp: 「少なくとも、今まで聞いたことはないな」
rows.en: “At least, I’ve never heard of it before.”

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Haven't heard about it 'till now at least."

rows.jp: 「……そういうものなのかな……いや、俺だって世代違うけど……」
rows.en: “...Huh. Maybe that really is how it works. I mean, it predates me too, but...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...that you would say something like... nah I'm from the wrong generation too, but..."
ghs.assessment: The English trails into an incomplete complement and does not convey the narrator's wondering realization that this may simply be how things are for a different generation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I guess that's just how it is... though I'm from a different generation too.'

highlights.text: that you would say something like

rows.jp: 「けど友貴、今の発言は昭和四十年代以降に生まれたすべてのパソコンおじさんたちを敵に回したぞ？」
rows.en: “Tomoki, you just made an enemy of every old-school computer geek born from 1965 onward.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "But Tomoki, that utterance right there just made you an enemy of every older PC user born after Showa 40, you get me?"

rows.jp: 「いや……今さらぜんぜん恐くないし……」
rows.en: “It’s not like I’m scared of them now...”

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Nah... I don't think there's annnything to be feared from them now..."

rows.jp: 「だいたい昭和なんて古生代に生まれたオールドタイプ１００％な原始人のことまでいちいち面倒見てられないよ」
rows.en: “Showa was basically the Paleozoic. I can’t be expected to babysit a bunch of certified, hundred-percent Old Type cavemen.”

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Besides, we can't take care of every single one of those 100% Old Type cavemen born in Paleozoic eras like Showa."

rows.jp: 「そんなこと言ったらダメェ～ッッッ！！」
友貴はわりと恐いもの知らずだ。

ghs.en: Tomoki is comparatively unaffected by terror.
ghs.assessment: The source plainly describes Tomoki as fairly fearless. The clinical abstraction is an unnatural calque and obscures the character judgment.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Tomoki is pretty fearless.'

rows.jp: 「そ、それが若いってことなんだろうな？　な？　無謀な若さって本当に恐いなあ、友貴よ」
rows.en: “S-So that’s youth, huh? Reckless youth is terrifying. Terrifying, Tomoki.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Th-, that's just a thing of youth, right? Right? Reckless youths really are scary, my dear Tomoki!"

rows.jp: 「だってさ……おじさんはおじさんコミュニティで得意のガン○ム話でも永遠にスパイラルさせておけばいいんじゃないかな？」
rows.en: “Why don’t the old guys stick to their old-guy circles and keep going around in circles about Gund*m forever?”

ghs.en: Tomoki: "'cause you know... wouldn't it be better to put the older men in old men communities where they can keep those discussions about Gun**m that they're so good at spiraling on endlessly?"

rows.jp: 「ひぃぃぃぃぃぃぃぃぃぃぃぃぃっ！？」

rows.en: That shaved years off my life.
